source_name: ISACA Slovenia Chapter (Slovenski odsek ISACA) — events list
why_relevant: Chapter events, CISA training cohorts and an annual international conference draw IT-audit, risk and compliance staff from Slovenian banks. Chapter board pages and event speaker listings expose current employers/titles of the audit-and-controls layer — a function banks staff up during regulatory build-outs (DORA, instant payments).

source_name: IIBA Slovenia Chapter — events and Balkan Business Analysis Conference
why_relevant: Business-analysis chapter (founded 2009) running webinars, the 'IIBA šola poslovno analitičnih pristopov' and a Balkan conference. Business analysts are a core hiring category in bank digital-transformation programmes; speaker and trainer bios reveal which banks are running BA-heavy projects and who leads them.

source_name: Večer Finančna konferenca (Financial Conference)
why_relevant: Long-running (37th edition) Slovenian financial conference run by the Večer media house, with programme strands on digitalisation of payment services and strategic change in the payments industry. Panel line-ups mix bank treasurers, CFOs and payment-service heads — good for both leadership moves and signals of new payment business units.

source_name: Delo Poslovni center (DPC) — konference (Mobilne tehnologije and related)
why_relevant: Delo's conference arm runs recurring digital/mobile-technology conferences whose panels include bank digital-channel and payments leadership. Programme pages carry named speakers with current titles and are published months ahead of the event.

source_name: Startup Slovenija / DIH Slovenia — FinTech Day and fintech events
why_relevant: FinTech Day and related events organised through the Slovenian startup ecosystem and the Digital Innovation Hub bring together fintech founders, bank innovation leads and investors. Attendee/speaker listings surface new Slovenian payments ventures and the bank staff seconded into innovation units.

source_name: AmCham Slovenia — events programme and Yearbook Dialogue
why_relevant: 450+ member companies and 100+ events a year, including business breakfasts and the AmCham Yearbook Dialogue (24-25 Sept 2026). Bank and payments executives appear as panellists; AmCham also publishes a yearbook of member-company leadership, which doubles as a directory of current C-level titles.

source_name: Zlata nit (Dnevnik) — best-employer award and finalist lists
why_relevant: Dnevnik's long-running (17+ editions) employer-of-the-year research, described as the largest of its kind in Europe, ranking small/medium/large employers. Banks and insurers (e.g. UniCredit Banka Slovenija, NLB, Zavarovalnica Sava) have appeared among entrants/finalists. Participation and category movement is a weak signal of employer-brand investment and imminent graduate/mass-hiring waves.

source_name: OTP banka Slovenija — Nagrade / Awards page
why_relevant: Bank-maintained list of awards received (The Banker 'Banka leta', Euromoney awards of excellence, best online bank, ESG category). Award pages name the winning unit and often the executive who accepted it, and reveal which business lines the bank is positioning as strategic — a leading indicator of where it invests headcount.

source_name: Ekonomska fakulteta UL — Karierni center (career centre) and job board
why_relevant: The main Slovenian economics/business faculty's career centre and its 'Delovna mesta' board carry employer-posted internships, graduate schemes and corporate-scholarship calls from banks. Because these postings often precede or replace public vacancy ads, they expose graduate-hiring waves and new team names that never reach job portals.

source_name: NLB — kadrovske štipendije / student programmes page
why_relevant: NLB's own student/scholarship page states the fields it sponsors (IT, data science, computer science, accounting) and that it partners with all major faculties. Changes in the sponsored-field list are an early, quiet indicator of where the group is building capability — e.g. a new data or payments-engineering track appearing before any vacancy is posted.

source_name: UL faculty career pages hosting bank scholarship calls (FE, FRI, FMF)
why_relevant: Individual University of Ljubljana faculties republish bank corporate-scholarship calls ('razpis za kadrovske štipendije') with the exact number of places, the target study programmes and the sponsoring bank. FMF/FRI also carry SID Banka scholarship calls for computational statistics and CS+maths masters students. This is the most granular quantified signal of planned graduate intake per bank.

source_name: IEDC–Bled School of Management
why_relevant: Slovenia's executive-education institution (founded 1986 by the Chamber of Commerce), running Executive MBA and Presidents' MBA cohorts. Participant profiles, alumni notes and custom-programme client lists identify senior Slovenian bankers in development pipelines — historically a strong precursor to promotion into executive roles.

source_name: Banka Slovenije — Napovednik dogodkov (central bank event calendar)
why_relevant: The central bank's public event calendar announces lectures, conferences and press events, with named speakers from Banka Slovenije and the supervised banks. It is a reliable pointer to upcoming sector gatherings where speaker rosters will be published, and directly names central-bank officials by current function.

source_name: Napovednik.com — Slovenian professional-event aggregator
why_relevant: General Slovenian event aggregator that indexes professional conferences and trainings (INFOSEK 2026 was listed there). Useful as a discovery layer to catch smaller banking/payments/IT events that have no standing presence in the sources above.

source_name: Knowledge Matters / Znanje šteje — international conference speakers
why_relevant: Slovenian-hosted international conference with a dedicated /govorci speakers page. Cross-sector, but historically features finance and management leadership; a secondary roster to diff for Slovenian financial-sector titles.

source_name: Slovenski marketinški kongres (SMK) — govorci
why_relevant: The main Slovenian marketing congress publishes a full speaker roster each edition. Bank CMOs, heads of digital channels and customer-experience leads speak here; marketing-side titles are often where new customer/payments propositions and their owners first surface publicly.

source_name: Davčno-finančna konferenca (DFK)
why_relevant: Recurring Slovenian tax-and-finance conference; programme features finance-function leadership including bank tax/treasury/compliance specialists. A narrow but stable secondary roster for tracking mid-senior finance titles.

source_name: PODIM Conference (Maribor) — startup/scaleup conference
why_relevant: The main Slovenian/CEE startup-investment conference. Slovenian fintech founders and bank corporate-venture representatives appear on its speaker list, which helps map new payments ventures and bank innovation-unit staff. NOTE: the canonical URL was inferred from general knowledge, not returned by my searches — treat as unverified until the liveness pass runs.

source_name: Sindikat bančništva Slovenije (SBS)
why_relevant: Representative sector trade union for banking in Slovenia (founded 1990, representative since 1993); signatory/negotiator of the Kolektivna pogodba dejavnosti bančništva Slovenije. Site lists constituent member unions at Deželna banka, Gorenjska banka, Intesa Sanpaolo, UniCredit, OTP and SID banka, and hosts statutes, legal-aid rules and collective-agreement documents. Primary channel for the downside of org change (branch closures, post-merger redundancies) and for pay/collective-bargaining disputes.

source_name: Sindikat finančnih organizacij Slovenije (SFOS) — ZSSS affiliate
why_relevant: The second representative union covering 'finančno posredništvo' (financial intermediation), affiliated to ZSSS, seat Dalmatinova 4, Ljubljana. Complements SBS: where SBS covers bank-level units, SFOS extends to insurance/leasing/other financial organisations. Its positions surface in sector bargaining and restructuring disputes.

source_name: Zveza svobodnih sindikatov Slovenije (ZSSS) — confederation site
why_relevant: Largest Slovenian union confederation, ~22 sector unions. Acts as a pointer/aggregator: publishes confederal statements, tripartite (Ekonomsko-socialni svet) positions, and links to each sector affiliate including SFOS. Useful to snowball actor map and to catch bank restructuring framed as a national labour issue.

source_name: Sindikat Nove Ljubljanske banke (Sindikat NLB)
why_relevant: House union at Slovenia's largest bank and a distinct bargaining actor: reporting indicates Sindikat NLB signed the 2026 tarifna priloga to the banking collective agreement while SBS refused. Tracking it separates employer-aligned from confrontational union positions and reveals NLB-internal staffing/branch decisions. No confirmed own website found — registry entry used as the anchor record.

source_name: Kolektivna pogodba dejavnosti bančništva Slovenije (PISRS register entry)
why_relevant: The authoritative consolidated text and amendment history of the banking-sector collective agreement on the state legal-information portal. Every renegotiation, tariff annex and change to redundancy/severance rules lands here, giving a dated, citable trail of bargaining outcomes.

source_name: Uradni list RS — collective agreements and tariff annexes (banking)
why_relevant: Official gazette where sector collective agreements and their tarifne priloge must be published together with the registration certificate (per ZKolP). Confirmed banking items: the 2024 tariff annex and the 2025 Kolektivna pogodba Banke Slovenije (central bank staff). Gives exact effective dates and signatory lists — the hard evidence behind union press claims.

source_name: Evidenca kolektivnih pogodb (MDDSZ register) via OPSI open-data portal
why_relevant: Machine-readable register of all collective agreements maintained by the labour ministry (MDDSZ) under Art. 25 ZKolP, published as an open dataset. Lets you enumerate every banking/finance agreement, its parties and its status without scraping — the structural backbone of the bargaining actor map.

source_name: Zavod RS za zaposlovanje (ZRSZ/ESS) — Trg dela v številkah
why_relevant: The public employment service publishes registered unemployment and reported job vacancies (sporočena prosta delovna mesta) by activity sector, 2005–2026. Because employers must notify ZRSZ 30 days before collective dismissals (ZDR-1 art. 98–99), sector-level inflows are the earliest quantitative echo of bank redundancies. Caveat: SKD 2025 replaced SKD 2008 from 1 Jan 2025, so series break — data are explicitly not comparable across that boundary.

source_name: ZRSZ Napovednik zaposlovanja (employment forecast survey)
why_relevant: Semi-annual employer survey in which firms state expected hiring and headcount reduction by activity; gives forward-looking signal on financial-sector staffing intentions ahead of any formal redundancy notice. Published as PDF reports with a stable naming pattern.
